item.text: {"case_id":"SPR00424","decision":"candidate","candidate_ranking":["C06","C12","C24"],"selected_candidate_label":"C06","confidence":0.99,"relationship_type":"both","rationale":"C06 is a clear substantive drafting template. The child adapts its Germany occupation framework to Austria: the High Commissioner remains the supreme United States authority and chief diplomatic official under the Secretary of State; the military commander continues to receive instructions from the Joint Chiefs of Staff; the commander acts at the High Commissioner's request to maintain order and protect United States interests; and an emergency exception permits action to safeguard troops. These distinctive provisions appear in substantially the same sequence and with closely corresponding language. C12 offers a weaker parallel for chief-of-mission authority and the separate Joint Chiefs command channel, while C24 supplies only the more general transfer-of-functions, property, records, and appropriations machinery.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"The United States High Commissioner for Austria shall continue to be the supreme United States authority in Austria, shall be the Chief of the United States diplomatic mission, and shall be responsible, under the immediate supervision of the Secretary of State, for the total governmental program of the United States in Austria, including representation of the United States in the Allied Commission for Austria","parent_excerpt":"The United States High Commissioner for Germany ... shall be the supreme United States authority in Germany. The High Commissioner shall have the authority, under the immediate supervision of the Secretary of State ... to exercise all of the governmental function of the United States in Germany ... including the representation of the United States on the Allied High Commission for Germany","explanation":"The child closely adapts the parent's central allocation of occupation authority, supervision, and Allied-commission representation from Germany to Austria."},{"child_excerpt":"with respect to military matters ... the Commanding General, United States Forces in Austria, shall continue to receive instructions directly from the Joint Chiefs of Staff","parent_excerpt":"With respect to military matters the Commander of the United States Armed Forces in Germany shall continue to receive instructions directly from the Joint Chiefs of Staff.","explanation":"This is nearly literal reuse of a distinctive military-command carveout."},{"child_excerpt":"On request of the High Commissioner ... the Commanding General shall take all necessary measures to protect United States interests in Austria and whatever action may be considered essential to preserve law and order and safeguard the security of United States troops and personnel.","parent_excerpt":"On request of the High Commissioner, such Commander shall take necessary measures for the maintenance of law and order and such other action as is required to support the policy of the United States in Germany. In the event of an emergency involving the security of the United States forces in Europe, such Commander may take whatever action he considers essential to safeguard the security of his troops.","explanation":"The child combines and adapts two consecutive parent provisions governing requested military support, preservation of order, and emergency protection of troops."}]}
